## PurchaseRepository

*class*

All SQL for the purchase_history table lives here and nowhere else.
The rest of the app never writes SQL against purchases; it calls these methods.

insert/find/spending methods manage their own connection. The Connection-accepting
overloads exist so PurchaseService can combine a purchase insert with an inventory_item
update (via store_item.store_item_item_id) in a single transaction; see openTransaction().

## PurchaseService

*class*

Business logic for purchases. No SQL here, no UI here.
Recording a purchase touches both purchase_history and the household's stock of the linked inventory_item,
so it runs both writes in one transaction: either both land or neither does.

## StockAmounts

*class*

Stock is counted in the catalogue item's own unit (g, ml, Stück), as the shopping list compares it with a line's unit.
A purchase is counted in packs, so one pack adds .perPack: the pack's size converted to the item's unit.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class finance_StockAmounts["StockAmounts"] {
        +perPack(int packSize, String packUnit, String itemUnit) int$
    }
```

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `int perPack(int packSize, String packUnit, String itemUnit)` | public static | How much of the item's unit one pack is: 500 g into an item counted in g is 500, 1000 g into an item counted in kg is 1. |

## StockService

*class*

Takes food out of a household's stock, in the item's own unit (g, ml, Stück). Using it and throwing it away are the same action: the
amount leaves the batch that expires first, the item's quantity goes down, and its earliest expiry date is worked out again from the batches that are left.
No SQL here. Everything runs in one transaction on the item's locked row.
